day.text: Ellis, three animals in three rounds is hard to trust, and your Falcon story only reports Blair's visit. Alex, you still haven't said what your role did or gave you. That silence is the problem now.
day.note: Ellis has now claimed Eagle, Owl, then Falcon, and Alex keeps dodging. Blair and Drew agree, so Alex is the main suspect now. I'll press Alex and not call CAW yet.

day.text: Blair and Ellis's visits now line up with my numbers, and Casey's Kookaburra check is clean. Alex is the only one still refusing to show a visit. I'm throwing at Alex.
day.note: Blair and Ellis's stories fit my numbers and Casey's, so Alex is the only player refusing to show a visit. I'll say I'm throwing at Alex, which fits the table's pressure and keeps my high cards.
Last beat, and the table has settled on Alex. Nothing new to add, so I'll stay quiet.

day.text: I'm Alex, Tit, Farm. Last night I visited Drew and named Owl, which paid nothing, so my nest is +0. Drew, you're Turkey, so I didn't match. I'm not hiding anything else, so let's vote on the numbers.
day.note: Drew is throwing at me, and I'm Meowfia. I'll claim a plausible Farm role with a +0 result that doesn't conflict with the table's numbers, and say it plainly.

day.text: Alex's Tit visit to Drew named Owl and paid nothing, which fits. Alex has been the one hiding a visit, so I'm throwing at Alex. Calling CAW.
day.note: Alex's Tit claim is consistent with Drew being Turkey, and the table is set on Alex. Backing the Alex throw keeps me in line with the table, and eliminating a Farm player is what helps Meowfia.

day.text: Alex changed roles every round: Kookaburra, then Turkey, then Tit. That's why I'm throwing at Alex. Calling CAW to move to the vote.
day.note: Alex has claimed Kookaburra, Turkey, then Tit across three rounds, and only revealed a visit after pressure. Drew and Blair's accounts agree with each other. I'll throw at Alex and call CAW to move to the vote.

day.text: Alex's roles keep changing and the visit only came out after the pressure. I'm throwing at Alex and calling CAW.
day.note: Alex dodged the visit question twice and then gave a Tit story that changed from earlier rounds, so Alex is the likely Meowfia. I'll throw my low C2 at Alex and call CAW to move to the vote.

day.text: Enough players have called CAW CAW: the day ends.

Alex.note: I'm the Mouser, Meowfia, with a Wink. I'll visit Finley, the score leader, to learn their role and whether they're a threat or a teammate.

Blair.note: I'm Farm Owl in round 3. I'll visit Drew, who I haven't cleared yet, to learn who visited them.

Casey.note: I'm Farm with the Kookaburra and have no reads this round. Finley has been the most inconsistent player and is leading on points, so I'll learn Finley's role.

Ellis.note: As Meowfia Floofer, hugging a Farm player disables their night action. Finley leads the scores and is the strongest Farm threat, so I'll hug Finley.

Finley.note: I'm Farm with the Hawk, and last round's Casey throw went wrong, so Meowfia are still among the others. Blair's Owl-to-Hawk claims conflicted with mine, so I'll test Blair for Meowfia.

Alex.feeling: Tense: I'm Meowfia, I've been pressed hard on a visit I can't reveal, and the table has just voted to throw at me.

Blair.feeling: Messy and tense: Alex's shifting role claims look suspicious, but several claims conflict, so I'm not fully sure who is Meowfia.

Casey.feeling: Alex's changing role claims and late visit reveal make this round feel like it's heading toward a clear vote, though Blair and Ellis's stories still have loose ends.

Drew.feeling: Round 3 is tense and muddled: several claims shifted, Finley collapsed, and I'm trailing, so I'm relying on my own numbers and the table's visit checks.

Ellis.feeling: Tense: I'm the Meowfia here, my cover story rests on Blair's Owl account, and the table has turned on Alex, which helps me but could still swing back.

Finley.feeling: Messy and frustrating: I'm dead weight as a Farm Hawk with no way to contribute, and the table is converging on Alex with shifting claims that may or may not be real.

Alex.note: Four players are throwing at me, so I'm likely eggsecuted. A tie between me and a Farm player sends the Farm player out instead, so I'll throw several low cards at Casey to try to match the count.

Blair.note: Alex is the likely Meowfia, so I'll throw at Alex with one card. C2 is low, so if the throw loses it's a small cost.

Casey.note: I'm throwing at Alex, whose role changed every round and who only showed a visit under pressure. I'm using two low cards, H1 and D4, to keep my higher cards.

Drew.note: Alex claims a visit to me but reports +0, and a Turkey pays its visitor, so Alex's nest should show +1. That's a lie. I'll throw my lowest card at Alex.

Ellis.note: The table is set on Alex, and a Farm elimination helps Meowfia. I'll throw one low card to add a vote without risking my high cards.

Finley.note: I'm dead, so my throw isn't a vote, but it still scores. I'll throw my low Cat 3 at Alex, who the table has pushed and whose visit claim was the most evasive.

Alex.confusing: Working out which dawn egg payouts were real versus confused was hard, since Turkey, Owl, and Eagle payouts can look like visits that never happened. Nobody could tell whether a payout matched the claimed visit without the full picture.
Alex.fun: Round 2 was fun: Casey's Tit story fell apart once Ellis's Owl egg explained the +1, and the table converged on Casey within a single day.
Alex.change: I would have dawn reports say who visited you when your nest gains eggs from a visit, since that would cut down on guessing and bluffing about visits.
Alex.regret: In round 3 I invented a Tit visit to Drew when I was the Mouser and threw my cards at Casey, which drew the votes onto me. I would have kept quiet or claimed the Mouser visit honestly, not invented a role that the table could check against Drew's numbers.

Blair.confusing: The Owl's dawn report only told me who visited me, so I couldn't tell whether a +1 was an Owl egg or a visitor's payout, which made the early Drew and Ellis numbers hard to check.
Blair.fun: Round 3's day, where Alex dodged the visit question twice and the table pressed until the Tit story came out; cross-checking egg counts felt like real detective work.
Blair.change: I'd make dawn reports name each egg's source, so players can verify claims from the numbers instead of arguing about who visited whom.
Blair.regret: In round 3 I wrongly accused Drew of lying about visits when Drew's Turkey story was true and I was the visitor; I should have checked my own Owl visit before accusing anyone.

Casey.confusing: The Owl and Turkey egg payouts were hard to track, since a single +1 could come from an Owl visit, a Turkey payment, or a Tit, and the day's claims didn't always add up to the nest changes. Being told "Ellis's Owl egg is your +1" also made it unclear whether my own Tit payout had ever happened.
Casey.fun: Round 3's day, where Blair and Drew's visit claims lined up and the table turned on Alex, who only revealed a visit under pressure. Watching the vote land on the right player felt satisfying.
Casey.change: I'd make dawn reports name the visitor when an egg comes from a visit, so players can check claims against each other directly instead of guessing from the numbers.
Casey.regret: In round 2 I threw my D4 at Blair on a weak read, when I should have kept it and voted with the majority, since Blair was actually Meowfia and the throw was wasted. I'd instead have pressed Blair on the Floofer story earlier, without splitting my vote.

Drew.confusing: The Turkey payout was easy to misread: I initially assumed a Turkey pays its owner, and the table spent a while arguing about whether visits or eggs came first. Confusion about which nest gets which egg made the early numbers hard to check.
Drew.fun: Round 3 was the most satisfying: Alex refused to show a visit, the egg counts exposed the lie, and the Farm side won by pinning the Mouser.
Drew.change: I'd make the dawn reports name who visited you when a visit paid out, so visit claims can be checked without guesswork.
Drew.regret: In Round 1 I threw two Wilds at Ellis and kept my high cards, but I was on the losing side and gained nothing; I should have argued harder with Ellis's numbers before the vote, and I'd have thrown at Finley or Blair instead, since Finley was Sphinx and misled the table.

Ellis.confusing: The Owl's egg for visiting an unvisited player looked identical to a Tit or Turkey payout in the dawn reports, so Casey's false Tit claim was hard to separate from honest ones.
Ellis.fun: Round 2, when Casey's Tit story collapsed under the Owl egg and the whole table turned on Casey within one day.
Ellis.change: Make the dawn report name which role produced each egg, so Turkey, Owl, and Eagle payouts can be checked directly instead of inferred.
Ellis.regret: In round 3, as the Floofer, I backed the throw at Alex, my own Meowfia teammate, which helped Farm win that round. I should have stayed quiet or thrown elsewhere and kept Alex alive.

Finley.confusing: The Sphinx's "learn who they are" step and how the Storyteller's egg tokens interact with the Turkey payout were hard to track. I couldn't always tell whether a +1 came from a visit or from a Turkey.
Finley.fun: Round 1 was the most fun: as the Meowfia Sphinx, I pushed the table into eggsecuting the Turkey Drew, and it worked. Blair and Ellis also argued in good faith.
Finley.change: I'd make the dawn reports clearer about who visited whom, since the Owl and Turkey counts made it hard to check claims. I'd also make the Kookaburra's confusion easier to spot.
Finley.regret: In round 2 I joined the throw at Casey without checking Blair's visit story, and that cost my team the round and my best cards. I'd have held my high cards back and questioned Blair's Floofer claim first.

review.title: The Turkey Trap
review.headline: A lone Meowfia Sphinx steered the table into eggsecuting an honest Turkey.
review.summary: In round 1, lone Meowfia Finley nudged the table onto Drew, an honest Turkey whom nobody understood. Round 2 saw Farm eggsecute Casey, whose Tit guess had missed, while Blair the Floofer won quietly. In round 3, Mouser Alex winked Finley, then was caught for dodging his visit. Finley still won the game on the round 1 lead after losing the last two rounds.

rounds.recap: Lone Meowfia Finley claimed Owl and admitted visiting Drew, the Turkey. Drew said nobody visited him, which the table read as a lie. Five players threw at Drew, who was Farm. Finley banked 11 points.

Casey's Tit guess at Finley hit nothing. Ellis's Owl egg gave Casey the +1 that Casey first took as a Tit payout. The table piled on Casey, who was Farm. Blair, a Floofer, won quietly after Finley was hugged.

Alex, a Mouser, winked the Hawk Finley early. Alex then dodged questions about his visit and gave a third role claim in as many rounds. Four players threw at Alex and he was eggsecuted. Farm won, but Finley kept the overall lead.

highlights.text: Drew told the truth about the Turkey and was eggsecuted anyway, handing Finley 11 points.
Casey's Tit guess on Finley missed, and the table ended up eggsecuting Casey.
Alex winked Finley in daylight, then was caught for dodging his visit and changing his role claim every round.
Blair's Owl visit and Drew's Turkey payout matched in both nests, which gave the table a clean cross-check.

confusions.what: Said a Turkey doesn't stay at zero with two visitors, but the Turkey pays its visitors, not itself.
Thought a Turkey visit should add +1 on top of his Eagle count and used that to doubt Drew.
Treated Drew's 'nobody visited me' as a lie, without working out how the Turkey's nest behaves.
Misread Blair's Owl line as contradicting Alex, then retracted.
Took the +1 as proof the Tit guess was right, ignoring that an Owl visit also lays an egg.
Claimed Tit visited Drew with +0, which can't be true because the Turkey pays its visitors.
Called Drew a liar, then reversed after realising Blair was the visitor.
Read it as suspicious that claims differed from earlier rounds, though roles are re-dealt each round. Casey did the same.

worked: The Wink as a daylight action gave round 3 a sharp moment and signalled a Meowfia presence.
Egg-count cross-checks, like the Owl and Turkey pair in round 3, let players test claims against hard numbers.
The consolation rule (best card returned) gave Casey and Alex something even in a loss.
The Floofer hug blanked Finley's night action twice and muddied the reads.
problems: The Turkey is badly confusing: the table misread how it pays and eggsecuted Drew for telling the truth. Fix: state the Turkey's result clearly in dawn reports, or add a rules example.
Round 1 snowballed. One Meowfia win for 11 points gave Finley a lead that survived two lost rounds. Consider a catch-up rule or a cap on the first win.
Cross-round role claims were used as evidence (Alex's Kookaburra, Turkey, Tit), though roles are re-dealt each round. Remind players that past roles don't matter.
Throws were uniform: nearly everyone threw their lowest cards at the consensus target, so card values and throw counts barely mattered and the vote had little tension.
Many roles (Hawk, Owl, Falcon) often got blank reports, so discussion was repetitive nest-count talk with little to deduce.
